items.title: Trump sends Vance, Witkoff, Kushner to Islamabad for Iran talks

featured_image.name: Iran War Latest: Vance, Witkoff, Kushner Heading to Pakistan for Peace  Talks - Bloomberg

items.description:
President Donald Trump is dispatching a high-level delegation led by Vice President JD Vance to Islamabad for face-to-face negotiations with Iran, the White House announced Wednesday, just hours after a fragile two-week ceasefire halted 38 days of U.S. and Israeli military operations against Tehran.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed the team. "I can announce that the president is dispatching his negotiating team, led by the vice president of the United States, JD Vance, Special Envoy Witkoff and Mr. Kushner to Islamabad for talks this weekend," she said. "The first round of those talks will take place on Saturday morning local time."[1]

items.title: Israel learned of Iran cease-fire deal at last minute

featured_image.name: Netanyahu says announcement of Gaza ceasefire's next phase is ...

items.description:
Israel was not formally part of the negotiations that produced the two-week cease-fire between the United States and Iran announced on Tuesday, and Israeli officials were unhappy to learn that a deal had been finalized without prior consultation, according to a Wall Street Journal exclusive report citing mediators and a person familiar with the matter.[1]

The extent of Israel's involvement amounted to a phone call from President Donald Trump to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shortly before the cease-fire was publicly announced, a White House official told the Journal. Netanyahu agreed to participate in the cease-fire during that call.[1]

items.title: Meta unveils Muse Spark, its first AI model from superintelligence team

items.description: Meta on Wednesday unveiled Muse Spark, the first artificial intelligence model produced by its superintelligence division, marking the company's most substantial AI release in over a year as it races to close a gap with rivals OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. The model, developed over roughly nine months under the internal codename Avocado, is now powering the Meta AI app and website in the United States, with a broader rollout planned in the coming weeks across Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, and Meta's smart glasses.[1][2][3]

items.title: Ceasefire frays as Iran strikes Gulf states, refinery hit

featured_image.name: Iran hits Kuwaiti oil refinery, blasts boom over Tehran

items.description:
The ink was barely dry on the two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran when fresh violence erupted across the Middle East on Wednesday, underscoring the fragility of an agreement reached just hours before President Trump's deadline threatening the destruction of Iranian "civilization."[1][2]

Iran launched a wave of missiles and drones at targets in the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait early Wednesday, claiming retaliation for a strike on its oil facilities, according to Al Jazeera. The UAE Defense Ministry said its air defenses were "actively engaging" Iranian ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones, while Kuwait reported intercepting 28 Iranian drones targeting oil facilities, power plants, and water desalination sites, with some causing infrastructure damage. Separately, Iran's state-owned refiner NIORDC confirmed that a 55,000-barrel-per-day refinery on Lavan Island was struck in what it called a "cowardly attack by enemies" around 10 a.m. local time Wednesday, though no casualties were reported.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Vance calls Iran ceasefire 'fragile,' set to lead talks Friday

featured_image.name: US proposes replacing Witkoff with JD Vance on negotiating team ...

items.description:
US Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday described the newly struck ceasefire between the United States and Iran as a "fragile truce," urging Tehran to negotiate in good faith and warning that President Donald Trump is "not one to mess around."

Speaking at the Mathias Corvinus Collegium in Budapest during a two-day visit to Hungary, Vance said Trump is "impatient to make progress" and that Iran faces serious consequences if it does not engage sincerely in upcoming talks.[1][2]

"If the Iranians are willing in good faith to work with us, I think we can make an agreement," Vance said. But he cautioned: if Iran refuses to come to the negotiating table, "they're going to find out that the President of the United States is not one to mess around".[1]
